rounds.text: Jinkushal Industries Ltd carries severe fundamental risks that are masked by top-line growth figures. The company's cash generation has collapsed entirely, evidenced by an operating cash flow of Rs -113 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -116 Cr in Mar 2026, leading to a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -9.42x [E27, E28, E29]. This cash drain has forced borrowings to nearly double from Rs 55 Cr to Rs 101 Cr over a single year [E32]. Operational efficiency is rapidly deteriorating as working capital days balloon from 60.6 days to 129 days, driven by alarming debtor collection periods of 253 days [E53, E54]. Profitability metrics are heading in the wrong direction, with trailing twelve-month profit growth plunging -20% and quarterly operating margins shrinking from 8% down to 2% in Mar 2026 [E19, E24]. Institutional confidence is also fracturing, highlighted by domestic institutions slashing their holdings from 8.95% to 4.23% in recent quarters [E36], while shareholders receive a 0.00% dividend yield despite reported profits [E4, E52]. The equity also carries extreme volatility of 95.3% alongside a historically punishing peak-to-trough drawdown of -61.3% [E45, E46]. Conceded: [E16].
